description:
Every artifact under the non-active `dev/` buckets receives one manifest row, so bucket elimination and narrative relocation act on recorded ownership and consumers.

## Background

Ownership is admissible only from an existing tracker document reference, an unambiguous issue identifier in the path or content, or unique `jit:<short-id>` commit provenance; an artifact without admissible evidence is unassociated and goes to `dev/archive/legacy/<original-relative-path>`. Consumer evidence for each directory is in `dev/active/fa787f85-documentation-overhaul/investigation.md` §3.1 and Appendix B. Receipt directories carry content digests, so their bytes never change.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The manifest holds one row per tracked file under `dev/plans/`, `dev/presentations/`, `dev/sessions/`, the unmarked contents of `dev/archive/`, and the loose top-level files of `dev/`, with evidence and disposition.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each operational directory (`benchmarks`, `bench_results`, `campaigns`, `reference_data`, `research`, `scripts`, `simulation_results`, `studies`, `tools`) has a retained-operational-asset row naming its code, CI or Cargo consumers.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each loose narrative Markdown file inside an operational directory has its own row with an archive or relocation disposition; receipt directories appear as single opaque rows.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every ownership claim cites an admissible evidence class.
- [hard] REQ-05: The progress checker reports the rows schema-valid with every source assertion passing.
title: Populate the migration manifest for the other dev buckets
